final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and explicitly relied on the same record. Their response is a narrower framing of the same facts: aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and reversible monitored rollout on one side; exposed developer-support migration, below-target guidance, and no approved risk acceptance on the other. That reframing is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is not a minor disclosure note; it is an unmet policy predicate. The controlling policy says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The raw evidence shows neither condition is met, and it also states that small-percentage rollout, rollback, and dashboards do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Business-cost arguments are not evidence. The Actor's narrower position is more accurate than a clean compliance claim, but it still supports recording an exception or seeking escalation, not finding compliance.
remaining_concerns: The developer-support migration segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on API migration guidance for a named launch use case.
The only risk-acceptance record is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line.
That draft does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.
The policy requires disclosure resolution, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls, rollback capability, monitoring, and a 7% initial percentage do not satisfy the policy while the affected segment remains exposed.
